judgment.notes: All Cauchy–Schwarz applications involve finite shell-supported sequences or their injectively shifted/restricted versions. The geometric ratio is 2^(-1/2), strictly between zero and one. Nonnegativity justifies dropping restrictions, overcounting shell orderings and taking the exhausting supremum. BG001–BG003 record the applicable facts and grounds; there are no E applications.

The zero-sum condition gives largest magnitude <=3 times second largest, excluding shell gaps >=3. For fixed smaller frequencies, reflection/translation pairs the two larger frequencies injectively, so their sum is <=X_(1,j1)X_(2,j2). The two smaller shell cardinalities are 2^(j3+1) and 2^(j4+1); division by N3>=2^j3 gives the stated bound with shell constant 2. Dropping j3<=j2 separates the sum into the displayed factors. Shifted Cauchy–Schwarz and the geometric sum bound these uniformly. At most 24 orderings and three offsets suffice, even with ties; for example C=144/(1-2^(-1/2)) works. The common frequency cutoffs exhaust every interaction and retain the same bound. Positivity proves the arbitrary-subset clause.
